ai.description: *Gerrhopilus andamanensis* is a slender, worm-like snake reaching 20 cm. It is uniform dark brown with a pale snout and tail tip. Key features include 18 midbody scale rows and a rounded head.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Gerrhopilus andamanensis* is distinguished from other Indian worm snakes by its unique combination of 18–20 midbody scale rows and a distinctively rounded, blunt snout.
ai.habitat: The Andaman worm snake inhabits moist, lowland tropical evergreen forests, typically found burrowing within leaf litter or decaying organic matter in the Andaman Islands.
ai.behavior: The Andaman worm snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending most of its life burrowing through moist soil and leaf litter in search of ant and termite larvae.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gerrhopilus andamanensis* is oviparous, laying small clutches of elongated eggs. While specific breeding data is limited, they likely reproduce during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Gerrhopilus andamanensis* is endemic to the Andaman Islands in the Bay of Bengal, occurring at low elevations within this tropical archipelago.
